gap: No result ChatGPT got states how many watts the bundled 200–220 W panels actually delivered in a named test. In OutdoorGearLab's side-by-side panel test (Sam Schild, 2026-07-13), EcoFlow's NextGen 220W averaged 193 W, Jackery's SolarSaga 200 averaged 171 W, an earlier Anker SOLIX PS200 averaged 166 W and Bluetti's 200W Portable averaged 150 W. Each panel ran for two hours into the same Jackery 1000.
standout_why: I opened five rival pages and none has measured panel or solar-input figures. Lights On Labs (cited) says it hasn't tested the units and works out its refill hours from rated panel watts. StormWatts (cited) says it hasn't tested hands-on and assumes 0.85 efficiency; its only observed result is the owner's own Explorer 2000 Plus with 800 W of panels (696 W peak, 17–100% in about 3.5 h), and that setup isn't one of the kits. SolutionEnergy (cited) has only maker specs and a 0.75 planning factor. PowerSized (cited) does give OutdoorGearLab's measured usable output for the AC180 (950 Wh) and Explorer 2000 v2 (1,710 Wh), so the usable-capacity half of this angle is already partly out there. But PowerSized says it found no published solar-charging test, and its recharge benchmarks assume 75% of panel rating. I couldn't fetch Good Housekeeping or PowerOutage.us (blocked and 403).
decides: This backs the EcoFlow DELTA 3-family kit (1,024 Wh + 220 W panel) as the budget pick over the BLUETTI AC180 + 200 W kit, which ChatGPT listed at $769 next to EcoFlow's $699–729. OutdoorGearLab measured 193 W from EcoFlow's 220 W panel against 150 W from Bluetti's 200 W panel, about 29% more. The usable-capacity test points the same way: OutdoorGearLab got 870 Wh (85%) from the DELTA 3 and 950 Wh (82%) from the AC180. So the AC180's extra 128 Wh on paper shrinks to 80 Wh at the outlet, and its kit panel refills more slowly. At the measured panel output, rated capacity divided by measured watts (ignoring charging losses) comes to about 5.3 h for the DELTA 3, 6.2 h for the C1000 Gen 2, 6.3 h for the Jackery 1000 v2 and 7.7 h for the AC180. At 2 kWh, the Explorer 2000 v2 with two 200 W panels gave 1,710 Wh usable (84%) and would take about 6.0 h at 2 × 171 W. One caveat: I couldn't confirm on EcoFlow's store page that the DELTA 3 Classic kit ships the same NextGen 220W panel OutdoorGearLab tested.
